plain.text: Accept those whose faith is weak, without arguing over disputed matters. One person's faith allows them to eat anything, but another, whose faith is weak, eats only vegetables. The one who eats everything must not look down on the one who does not, and the one who does not must not judge the one who does, for God has accepted them. One person considers one day more sacred than another; another considers every day alike. Each should be fully convinced in their own mind. Whatever we do, we do for the Lord. Whether we live or die, we belong to the Lord. So why judge one another? We will all stand before God's judgement seat.

Stop passing judgement. Instead, decide never to put a stumbling block in your brother's or sister's way. Paul is convinced that nothing is unclean in itself, but if someone regards something as unclean, then for them it is unclean. If your food upsets another believer, you are no longer acting in love. "For the kingdom of God is not a matter of eating and drinking, but of righteousness, peace and joy in the Holy Spirit." Make every effort to do what leads to peace and to building each other up. Whatever you believe about these things, keep between yourself and God. Everything that does not come from faith is sin.

summary.bigIdea: In matters where believers disagree, accept one another, don't judge, and put love and peace first.
points: Believers may differ over food and special days; each should act in good conscience before God.
Do not judge or look down on one another; we all belong to the Lord.
The kingdom of God is about righteousness, peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.
summary.reflection: Is there a disagreement where you could choose to accept someone rather than judge them?
